Locate points in a triangle pool

Source: R/tri_ops.R
tri_locate.Rd

The triangle that holds each point: point in polygon (ST_Intersects() or ST_Contains() of a point) answered by point location on the mesh.

Usage

tri_locate(x, at)

Arguments

x

A wkpool_tri.

at

The points: any geometry wk::wk_handle() understands (its vertices are used, as wk::wk_coords() gives them), a two-column matrix, or a data frame or list with x and y.

Value

An integer vector with one triangle row of x per point, NA where no triangle holds it.

Details

Triangles are bucketed on a uniform grid over the extent of the mesh, and each candidate is tested with an exact orientation sign, so a point on an edge or a vertex is decided the same way for every triangle that holds it, and goes to the lowest triangle row among them. A point inside no triangle, or with a missing coordinate, is NA. Triangles may be either orientation; a degenerate triangle (zero area) holds no point.

The feature of the polygon each point falls in is pool_feature(x)[tri_locate(x, at)], and the group of any grouping (as in tri_measures()) is found the same way.

Examples

v <- data.frame(.vx = 1:6, x = c(0, 1, 1, 0, 2, 2), y = c(0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1))
tri <- new_wkpool_tri(v, vx0 = c(1, 1, 2, 2), vx1 = c(2, 3, 5, 6),
                      vx2 = c(3, 4, 6, 3), feature = c(1, 1, 2, 2))
pts <- wk::xy(c(0.75, 0.25, 1.5, 3), c(0.25, 0.75, 0.5, 0.5))
i <- tri_locate(tri, pts)
i
#> [1]  1  2  3 NA
## the feature each point falls in
pool_feature(tri)[i]
#> [1]  1  1  2 NA
